responsibility: Provides the stable external-facing model and query surface for compiler internals by exposing a versioned representation of items, types, and MIR that tools can inspect through the active compiler context. The crate root (`lib.rs`) establishes this public API surface: it wires together the crate’s modules, re-exports core definitions and errors, defines fundamental crate-wide entities such as crates, items, symbols, and opaque values, and offers top-level entry points for querying the current compilation. `error.rs` supplies the shared error model and formatting/utilities used across that API so requests and compiler-execution failures can be reported consistently. The type side of the interface is centered in `ty.rs`, which defines StableMIR’s type-system data model and type-oriented queries, covering interned types and constants, generics, predicates, trait references, ADTs, callable forms, and compiler-backed queries for layouts, ABI, and constant evaluation; `visitor.rs` complements this with the generic visitor framework for recursively traversing those type-level structures. On the MIR side, `mir.rs` is the entry point for the MIR subsystem, organizing allocation, body, monomorphization, pretty-printing, and visitation support and re-exporting the main MIR APIs. Its `mir` module then provides the actual StableMIR MIR representation and inspection layer: it defines MIR bodies and control-flow, exposes the monomorphized-item interface for resolving instantiated functions and statics to MIR and related codegen-oriented queries, and supplies the immutable walking/visitor machinery for systematically traversing MIR. Together, these pieces make `stable_mir` the crate that translates rustc’s internal compilation state into a stable, inspectable API for tools that need consistent access to items, types, and MIR.
